verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is scheduled to splash down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California'; R2: 'off the coast of San Diego, California'; R3: 'splashdown in the Pacific Ocean at 8:07 p.m. ET off San Diego'; R4: 'Pacific Ocean'; R5: 'Pacific Ocean'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state the splashdown location as Pacific Ocean off San Diego, California.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is scheduled to splash down on Friday, April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Friday, April 10'; R2: 'Friday, April 10, 2026'; R3: 'Friday evening'; R4: 'Friday, April 10'; R5: 'Friday'
verifications.reasoning: Sources consistently confirm the date as Friday, April 10, 2026.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is scheduled to splash down at approximately 8:07 p.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources directly specify approximately 8:07 p.m. ET/EDT for splashdown.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II landing time is estimated at 8:07 p.m. EDT / 5:07 p.m. PDT on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1/R2/R3/R5: '8:07 p.m. ET' on 'April 10'; R2: 'April 10, 2026'; R4: '8:07 p.m. EDT on Friday, April 10'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly confirm 8:07 p.m. EDT/ET and April 10, 2026; 5:07 p.m. PDT is the exact 3-hour conversion, precisely matching the attributed time.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft will re-enter Earth’s atmosphere at roughly 24,000 mph.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'nearly 24,000 mph'; R5: 'approximately 23,864 miles per hour'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state re-entry speed as nearly/exactly ~24,000 mph, matching 'roughly'.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is a 10-day lunar flyby mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: '10-day journey around the moon'; R3: '10 days in space'; R5: '10-day... journey around the moon'; R1: context of nine days elapsed toward 10-day total
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly describe it as a 10-day lunar flyby mission.

verifications.claim: U.S. Navy and NASA personnel will secure the capsule and retrieve the crew.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'U.S. Navy recovery vessel... Navy divers attaching devices... secure it'; R2: 'U.S. Navy recovery vessel... NASA's Johnson Space Center'; R3: 'U.S. Navy will assist with recovery'; R5: 'USS John P. Murtha'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm U.S. Navy and NASA involvement in securing capsule and retrieving crew.

verifications.claim: The capsule will experience a roughly 6-minute communication blackout due to plasma buildup during re-entry.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'communications blackout... as plasma builds up... around six minutes'; R1: 'superheated charged particles known as plasma will build up... block communications'
verifications.reasoning: R3 directly states ~6-minute plasma blackout; R1 supports plasma cause.

verifications.claim: Parachutes will deploy in stages to slow the capsule to roughly 20 mph for splashdown.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'parachutes to deploy... two smaller drogue... three small... three main parachutes... to just 17 mph'; R2: similar stages 'to just 17 mph'; R3: 'three main parachutes... to around 20 mph'
verifications.reasoning: Sources detail staged parachute deployment slowing to ~17-20 mph, matching 'roughly 20 mph'.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew consists of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Reid Wiseman... Christina Koch... Victor Glover... Jeremy Hansen'; R2/R3: identical crew listing
verifications.reasoning: All sources list exactly these four crew members.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will be extracted by helicopter and taken to a Navy vessel.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'airlifted onto a U.S. Navy recovery vessel'; R2: 'hoisted up into a helicopter basket for transport to the naval vessel'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly describe helicopter extraction to Navy vessel.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is designed to test critical systems for future Artemis moon landings.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'paving the way for a potential moon landing in 2028... tested out their gear while conducting manual piloting demonstrations'; R3: 'Every system we’ve demonstrated... life support, navigation, propulsion, communications'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm testing systems to enable future moon landings, directly supporting design purpose.
